summary: Synthetic GLM-5.2-shaped (glm_moe_dsa) native CUDA decode/prefill throughput vs context length on one A100 (40 GB), index-topk=256. Two collected points measure how the DSA decode/prefill paths scale with prompt length; this is NOT the real 753B GLM-5.2 model.
scope_note: 'optimistic-lower-bound' is the glm-throughput/1 tool's own token, preserved verbatim: this synthetic 8-layer dense wiring is a lower bound on the WORK the real 753B MoE must do, so the tok/s here are an optimistic UPPER bound on real-model speed (a lower bound on its latency). Do not read them as real-model throughput.

box.gpu: 1x NVIDIA A100 (40 GB, sm_80), one card of an 8-GPU datacenter server
box.note: A peer job held ~35 GB resident-but-idle (0% util) on every card at run time; the ~2-3 GB microbench runs on the ~5 GB free. Mirrors manifest.json box{}.

curve.reason: O(n^2) prefill x 5 reps ~= 15-20 min/point under the un-optimized synthetic kernel; aborted to free the shared GPU. No numbers collected.

derived.note: Derived purely from the two collected points above.

limitations: Only two context points (128, 512) were collected; the 2048 point was aborted for cost. A two-point curve shows direction, not a fitted scaling law.

An earlier same-node size sweep (varying layers/hidden) produced additional points, but its raw records lived only on the box and were deleted during cleanup, so they are deliberately NOT transcribed here (no reconstruction from memory).
Synthetic weights, 8 layers, dense FFN (no MoE), NOT the 753B GLM-5.2. Numbers characterize the CUDA decode/prefill wiring and its context scaling, not model quality or real-model throughput.
